purpose: ADDITIVE conformance vectors for action_ref v2 (domain-separated derivation), scoped to the live post-Domain-enforcement profile (see docs/spec/action-ref.md's Domain paragraph, effective 2026-07-29). Does NOT replace or narrow the live v1 fixture set at this same profile -- a v2-conformant verifier against this profile MUST still pass the live v1 domain-negative vectors. This is NOT a claim about the historical action-ref-v1.0 tag's own vector set (frozen before Domain enforcement, permissive on non-ASCII fields and empty scope) -- the two profiles disagree on some inputs by design, and results against each must be reported separately, never aggregated into one pass/fail count. Each vector here pairs the v1 hash (unchanged derivation) with the v2 hash (same four fields, domain tag prepended before hashing, 'v2:' prefix on the result) for the identical preimage, showing the two derivations differ for these three pinned preimages. validate.py additionally carries a defensive digest-equality assertion for the general case, which is a property no vector in this file (or any normally-constructed vector) can actually exercise -- see validate.py's module docstring.

vectors.description: NEXUS oracle signal example — same preimage as the worked v1 example already published in docs/spec/action-ref.md ('Serialization — JCS' section). v1 value here is copied from that published example, not recomputed, to prove this fixture is grounded in the live spec.
Memory write example — same preimage as the worked v1 example already published in docs/spec/action-ref.md ('Memory provenance attestation' section).
Synthetic third vector (payment.send), not tied to a prior published example, to avoid the fixture set relying on only two reused cases.

version_marker_conformance.note: A conformant verifier determines the derivation from the action_ref string's own grammar, never from context, assumption, or length/prefix alone.
version_marker_conformance.rule: action_ref_version(s): 'v1' if s matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ (64 lowercase hex chars); 'v2' if s matches ^v2:[0-9a-f]{64}$; ValueError otherwise. A same-length string with uppercase hex or non-hex characters matches neither and must raise, not be misread by length/prefix alone.

version_marker_negative_vectors.description: uppercase hex, 64 chars — same length as a valid v1 digest but not lowercase, must raise ValueError, not be misread as v1
non-hex characters, 64 chars — same length as a valid v1 digest but not hex, must raise ValueError, not be misread as v1
